- (m) Since any extension beyond the said statutory ceiling can be ordered only by this Commission in exercise of its regulatory powers, the Petitioner has been compelled to institute the present Petition, inter alia, seeking extension of time for injection of infirm power along with extension of FTC approval.

- (n) In terms of the proviso to Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code, the present Petition ought ordinarily to have been instituted at least fifteen (15) days prior to the expiry of the earlier approved period for injection of infirm power. In this backdrop, the Petitioner seeks relaxation and condonation of the intervening delay. The said delay has occurred for bona fide and procedural reasons. The present Petition was filed on 06.07.2026 after a delay of 6 days; thus, the Petitioner seeks condonation of delay in filing the instant petition under the Commission’s power to relax.

_“The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed inter alia seeking extension of time for injection of infirm power along with extension of First Time Charging (FTC) approval, for test run and commissioning in respect of the balance 42 MW capacity forming the part of the Petitioner’s Barmer Solar Project. # **<u>Submission of Petitioner in Compliance with the RoP for hearing dated 22.07.2026:</u>**

**4.** The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 07.08.2026 in its submission in compliance with the RoP for the hearing dated 22.07.2026, has mainly submitted as under:

- (d) The Petitioner has furnished the copy of commissioning certificates dated 14.03.2026, 27.03.2026 and 26.06.2026.

- (f) In view of the corrected position, the present Petition, though earlier described as being confined to the balance "42 MW" capacity, is, in fact and in correct terms, confined and restricted to the balance 38.1 MW capacity forming part of the 221 MW tranche of the Petitioner's Barmer Solar Project, and the reliefs sought in the present Petition, including the interim prayer, ought to be read and understood accordingly, i.e., as being confined to 38.1 MW and not 42 MW.

(iv) Pass such other and further order(s), direction(s), and relief(s) as this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice.

_“At the outset, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner is seeking an extension of 90 days for injection of infirm power along with extension of FTC approval, for test run and commissioning in respect of the balance capacity forming the part of the Petitioner’s Barmer Solar Project and the grounds for seeking such extension have been indicated in the affidavit filed by the Petitioner. He further added that the extension ought to be granted from the date of the Commission's final order._

_2. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the matter was reserved for order.”_

**10.** The Petitioner is seeking an extension of time to inject infirm power for a period of 90 days to carry out trial run and commissioning. Further, the Petitioner has submitted that in terms of proviso (b) of Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code, the present Petition should have been filed 15 days prior to expiry of the earlier approved period of infirm injection. The present Petition was, however, filed on 06.07.2026, with a delay of 6 days; therefore, the Petitioner has also sought condonation of the delay in filing the instant petition.

**11.** We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondent and the documents placed on the record.

**Issue 1:  Whether the delay in filing the instant Petition can be condoned? Whether the Petitioner can be granted an extension of time to inject infirm power for the balance capacity of 38.1 MW?**

**18.** The Petitioner has prayed for the condonation of the delay of 6 days in filing the instant Petition.

**19.** Considering the submissions of the Petitioner, we condone the delay in filing the instant Petition. Further, we note that the Petitioner is at an advanced stage of commissioning of its project and has already declared COD for 200 MW out of 250 MW solar project. Bihar State Power (Holding) Company Limited,** Vidyut Bhawan, Bailey Road, Patna – 781 001, Bihar. The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 29.11.2024, had submitted the statement showing the computation of IDC, and the discharge of IDC liability up to the date of commercial operation (COD). Accordingly, the drawl of loan prior to the Scheduled Commercial Operation Date (SCOD), i.e., 1.6.2019, was considered for the purpose of the computation of IDC. The said submission was taken on record while passing the order dated 15.1.2026 in Petition No. 498/TT/2025. 2. The Petitioner vide letter dated 5.5.2026, has admitted that the drawl date of loan “ _Commercial-335 SBI 04 (2018-19) (Q2)”_ was inadvertently mentioned as “3.9.2019” in place of “3.9.2018” in the statement with respect to Asset-3, showing IDC discharged up to the COD filed along with the supporting documents. Due to the above, there has been a consequential impact on the tariff components and the AFC trued-up with respect to Asset-3 for the 2019-24 and determination of tariff for the 2024-29 tariff period. Accordingly, the said inadvertent error is required to be rectified in exercise of the powers vested in the Commission under Regulation 54 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations 2023. Accordingly, we hereby rectify the inadvertent error occurring in various paragraphs of the order dated 15.1.2026 in Petition No. 498/TT/2025.
